title: Shared public and encrypted Nostr request/result lifecycle contract
intent: Standardize Bahia public, DNS, encrypted browser, and operator Nostr command lifecycles so command completion is driven by correlated terminal result events rather than status progress, polling, or timeout-only behavior.
observed_behavior: Public helper awaitResult already required scoped result filters and at least one accepted relay OK, but callers could pass status kinds as result kinds.
LLM deploy and rollback browser helpers treated kind 6973 status events as acceptable awaitResult completion candidates.
DNS status and result handling was separate but published before status/result subscriptions were opened.
Encrypted result handling subscribed before publish and required accepted OK, but accepted decrypted results without a request_event_id and reported AUTH closures after all-relay closure logic.
intended_behavior: Clients build/sign request events, open scoped result/status subscriptions before publish where the local request id is known, then publish and verify at least one accepted OK.
Status events are progress-only and must not satisfy terminal completion.
Terminal completion requires a result kind correlated to the request event id and requester; encrypted results require matching cleartext tags and decrypted request_event_id.
Zero accepted OK, AUTH, CLOSED, explicit abort, and configured timeout outcomes are distinct lifecycle failures or degraded waits, not implicit success.
